about.title: Prototype note
about.text: This tool supports practical sailing instruction. It is not a replacement for onboard safety briefings, local rules, boat-specific procedures, instructor judgement or weather decisions.

pointsOfSail.title: Points of Sail
pointsOfSail.learningGoal: Understand how wind direction and boat heading determine point of sail and basic sail trim.
pointsOfSail.dragHint: Tap the boat and drag left or right to rotate it.
pointsOfSail.buttonsTitle: Jump to a point of sail

noGo.label: Into wind / No-go zone
noGo.facts: The bow is too close to the wind. The sails cannot create useful drive and the boat may slow, stop or drift sideways.
noGo.bridge: Wind on your nose or both cheeks. A small flag would stream straight back over the deck. If you keep trying to sail here, the boat feels weak and noisy.
noGo.trim: Do not trim harder to fix this. Bear away first until the sails can fill. Then trim in again for close-hauled or close reach.

closeHauled.label: Close-hauled
closeHauled.facts: This is the closest practical course to the wind. You are sailing upwind, but not directly into it.
closeHauled.bridge: Wind on the front cheek. Looking forward, the wind feels forward and slightly to one side. A flag points aft but still pulls strongly from ahead.
closeHauled.trim: Mainsail and headsail are trimmed in tight. Keep the sail just full, not luffing. If the inside tell-tales lift or the luff shakes, you may be too high or under-trimmed.

closeReach.label: Close reach
closeReach.trimShort: Eased slightly, still inside the boat’s bounds
closeReach.facts: The boat has turned away from close-hauled. The sails can be eased a little and the boat often feels faster and more comfortable.
closeReach.bridge: Wind still forward, but less on the nose. It feels more like the wind is crossing your forward shoulder than hitting your face directly.
closeReach.trim: Ease the sails slightly, but keep them within the visual bounds of the boat. They should not be dumped out. Trim until the front edge just stops lifting.

beamReach.label: Beam reach
beamReach.facts: The wind is coming from the side of the boat. This is often one of the easiest and clearest points of sail to feel.
beamReach.bridge: Wind on your ear or directly on the side of your face. A flag would stream sideways across the boat.
beamReach.trim: Sails are about halfway out. If the front of the sail luffs, sheet in a little. If it feels over-tight and stalled, ease a little.

broadReach.label: Broad reach
broadReach.facts: The wind is coming from behind the side of the boat. The boat is moving downwind, but not dead downwind yet.
broadReach.bridge: Wind behind your ear or across the back corner of your neck. A flag streams forward and out to the opposite side.
broadReach.trim: Ease the mainsail until it approaches the spreader/shroud limit. Watch for a horizontal crease or ugly twist as the sail presses against rigging. Do not force it harder into the spreaders.

deadRun.label: Dead run
deadRun.facts: The wind is almost directly behind the boat. It can feel calm on deck, but the boom can gybe violently if the wind crosses the stern.
deadRun.bridge: Wind behind your head. The boat may feel quieter because you move with the wind. A flag points forward over the bow.
deadRun.trim: Main is far out. Watch the boom, keep people clear, and avoid accidental gybes. Later modules will cover preventers, gybe angles and safer downwind courses.
